reconcile.connective: Clarke resolves the apparent clash by reading Matthew's angel-and-stone scene as completed before the women arrived, not something they witnessed.

discrepancy.connective: D. F. Strauss names this a genuine contradiction, noting that even the harmonists' best fix requires straining Matthew's Greek rather than reading it plainly.

skeptic.name: D. F. Strauss
skeptic.work: The Life of Jesus Critically Examined
skeptic.attribution: D. F. Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846)

excerpts.excerpt_text: They found the stone rolled away - An angel from God had done this before they reached the tomb, Mat 28:2:
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke explicitly places the angel's stone-rolling recorded at Matthew 28:2 chronologically before the women's arrival, directly harmonizing it with Luke's (and by extension Mark's and John's) report that the women found the stone already rolled away.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's harmonized resurrection-narrative summary (adopting Robinson's reconstruction, pp. 327-329) places the earthquake, the angel's descent, and the rolling away of the stone before the women's arrival, so that 'on their arrival they find the stone already taken away.'
